# Electrical modelling sources

Checked **17 Sep 2026**. The following official pages were retrieved and their
relevant content reviewed. Summaries are original paraphrases, not reproduced
standard tables. The check date is not a publication or legal commencement date.

## E1 — U.S. Access Board: operable parts

- URL: https://www.access-board.gov/ada/guides/chapter-3-operable-parts/
- Checked: 17 Sep 2026; official HTML retrieved.
- Relevance: operable portions, clear floor space, approach orientation and
  intervening obstructions must be considered together. This supports keeping
  plate-centre measurements separate from operable-part reach and refusing to
  equate an in-range height with an unobstructed approach.
- Applicability limits: guidance explains U.S. ADA scoping, exceptions and
  technical requirements. It is not an Indian private-dwelling rule, universal
  socket-height profile, electrical protection specification or access-route solver.
  Read the applicable context before importing any numerical value.

## E2 — U.S. Access Board: entrances, doors and gates

- URL: https://www.access-board.gov/ada/guides/chapter-4-entrances-doors-and-gates/
- Checked: 17 Sep 2026; official HTML retrieved.
- Relevance: maneuvering needs depend on approach direction, door swing and
  hardware conditions. Clear passage measurements relate to physical door
  position rather than simply a nominal leaf or wall aperture dimension.
  This informs separate leaf-sweep, latch-side and approach checks.
- Applicability limits: U.S. accessible-route guidance, not automatic local legal
  applicability. A room rectangle and a quarter-circle do not establish hardware
  operability, complete accessible routes or compliance.

## E3 — UK Health and Safety Executive: electricity FAQs

- URL: https://www.hse.gov.uk/electricity/faq.htm
- Checked: 17 Sep 2026; official HTML retrieved.
- Relevance: competence is specific to the electrical task; wet/damp environments
  warrant additional scrutiny and protective devices are not comprehensive
  protection against every shock mechanism. Use this to justify professional
  review and the distinction between water-exposure context and spatial fit.
- Applicability limits: UK occupational-safety context, not Indian residential
  design authority. The retrieved FAQ still cites the seventeenth edition of
  BS 7671 in places. Do not treat those references as proof of the current
  applicable edition, or extract device ratings or installation instructions.

## Access and authority boundaries

No paywalled standard was reproduced or treated as fully reviewed. These sources
do not establish current CEA/BIS provisions, local adoption, bathroom zones,
product ratings or site-specific electrical approval. Request the applicable
current documents and qualified review before an engineering-sizing task.
The repository's earlier source registry is context, not fresh verification
of every URL or standard it lists. Public research must not include private
repository content, site coordinates, live plans or user records.
